label: rare: first copy step (echoed first token, mostly f/h/e/i/o/u/g), no identifiable selector
explanation: Extremely sparse (83 active steps in 6.5M on dev). About 72% of activation mass is at step L+1 (recall_idx 1, previous input <DEL>, input = echoed first original token). The echoed token is usually one of f, h, e, i, o, u, g, and long sequences (L=9) are over-represented. The other ~18% falls in the original phase at t=3..6, often on a token right after an i (e.g. the digit 1 after i). Activations are weak (max 0.19), and the largest ones are also at recall_idx 1. Precision stays below 1%: fewer than 1 in 1000 matching steps fire, and adding token-history conditions (i, j, v in the original) did not find what selects them. It never fires at t<3, on the delimiter step, or at recall_idx >= 3.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=h (+2.41), in_tok=e (+2.12), orig3=v (+2.04), phase=0 & in_tok=1 (+2.04), orig0=u (+2.01), orig3=i (+1.91). Lower it: orig8=- (-0.98), in_count=1 (-0.84), orig6=- (-0.40), orig7=- (-0.19).
